lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: handwashing and surface cleaning

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 3: Kitchen Care and Food Safety
objective: Learners perform a timed 20-second soap handwashing routine and an overlapping-stroke counter-wipe technique, then run a second quick water-only rinse and explain why the quick rinse does not remove germs the way the full wash does even though hands may look equally clean.
scenario: Before doing any food task, the learner is asked to demonstrate the household's full handwashing routine and a proper counter-wipe technique, timing the wash against the 20-second food-safety standard, then compares that wash to a quick rinse with no soap.
materials: a sink with soap and water
a clean towel or paper towel
a kitchen counter or clean table surface
a clean cloth or paper towel for wiping

tasks.directions: Before washing, predict how long 20 seconds actually feels like.

prompts.text: Guess how many seconds you think you usually spend washing your hands right now, without timing yourself.

tasks.directions: Wash your hands at the sink using soap, scrubbing the front, back, and between your fingers for a full 20 seconds timed on a clock, then wipe a kitchen counter or table surface using a clean cloth in overlapping strokes.

prompts.text: I used soap and scrubbed my hands, including between my fingers and around my thumbs, not just my palms.
I timed myself for the full 20 seconds instead of stopping early.
I wiped the counter or surface using overlapping strokes so no spot was missed.

tasks.directions: Now do a second, quick rinse of your hands with water only, no soap, for about 3 seconds, and compare how each wash felt.

prompts.text: Explain why a 3-second water-only rinse does not remove germs the way a full 20-second soap wash does, even though your hands might look and feel clean after both.
Name one specific moment today or this week when you would have used the quick rinse instead of the full wash if you had not practiced this.

tasks.directions: Think about surfaces compared to hands.

prompts.text: Explain one way that wiping a counter is similar to washing your hands for food safety, and one way it is different.

remediation: If a learner scrubs only their palms and skips between their fingers and around their thumbnails, reteach using a visible marker: rub a dot of washable marker on the back of one hand and between two fingers before washing, then check under a light whether the marker is fully gone after the 20-second wash.
extension: Have the learner time and compare wiping the same counter with a dry cloth only versus a cloth dampened with soapy water, then explain in writing which method actually lifted more visible crumbs or residue and why.
